title: Greeks, bump conventions and sensitivity tests

objectives.text: State delta,gamma,vega,rho and calendar-theta derivative units and signs before translating model sensitivities into finite bump/position approximations.
Compare analytic smooth-domain Greeks with central finite differences over several valid bump scales,distinguishing truncation,cancellation,kinks and model/market risk.
Compute the declared call price,delta,gamma and vega over the public smooth domain with explicit vega units,tail handling and six-decimal zero display.

blocks.markdown: A Greek is a local derivative of a specified model while other inputs are held fixed. Delta=dV/dS;gamma=d²V/dS²;vega=dV/dsigma;rho=dV/dr. We use calendar theta=-dV/dtauwith tauremaining YEARS,so positive elapsed calendar time decreases tau. A sensitivity is not a guarantee of an exact realized price change:several inputs can move,derivatives change,and the model can miss market behavior. Name stock-price/volatility/rate scenario rules when comparing Greeks;sticky strike versus other volatility-surface rules are not interchangeable.

Per-underlying-unit option prices here use delta in option-price currency per1currency spot move,gamma per squared spot-currency unit,vega per absolute volatility1.0,rho per annual-rate1.0,and theta per YEAR of elapsed time. One percentage-point volatility bump is0.01,so multiply vega_per_1by0.01. One basis-point rate bump is0.0001,so multiply rho_per_1by0.0001. A rough per-calendar-day theta is theta_per_year/365ONLY under that named day convention/local approximation. Position PnL also needs signed contract count and contract multiplier;do not confuse per-unit values with per-contract exposure.

blocks.title: Percent points,basis points and local PnL

For a small spot move dS,delta-gamma approximation is dV≈delta*dS+0.5*gamma*dS². Long2contracts with multiplier100multiply per-unit dVby200. A short position changes the sign. This does not include changing volatility,rates,time,fees or model error.

blocks.markdown: For this no-dividend call smooth domain,use phi(d1)=exp(-d1²/2)/sqrt(2*pi). Delta=N(d1);gamma=phi(d1)/(S*sigma*sqrt(tau));vega_per_1=S*phi(d1)*sqrt(tau);rho_per_1=K*tau*D*N(d2);calendar theta/year=-S*phi(d1)*sigma/(2*sqrt(tau))-r*K*D*N(d2). Put delta=-N(-d1),same gamma/vega,put rho=-K*tau*D*N(-d2),put calendar theta=-S*phi(d1)*sigma/(2*sqrt(tau))+r*K*D*N(-d2). Our code exposes CALL Greeks only;these stated put identities are transfer material,not an unimplemented put-Greek API.

For spot bump h>0,central delta≈[V(S+h)-V(S-h)]/(2h);gamma≈[V(S+h)-2V(S)+V(S-h)]/h². Central vega/rho use analogous symmetric volatility/rate bumps in their DECIMAL units. Calendar theta≈-[V(tau+h)-V(tau-h)]/(2h),with hyears. Both sides must stay in supported smooth domain and represent the same contract/held-fixed rules. Otherwise reject or use a documented one-sided/limit method with different error properties,not an accidental negative-vol/time call.

In a smooth region central first differences have O(h²)truncation under the needed derivatives. Reducing hfirst improves approximation,but subtracting nearly equal floating prices amplifies rounding error,roughly eps/hfor first differences and eps/h²for second. A smaller bump is not always better. Inspect a sweep of bump sizes against an independent analytic/reference result and report the region where results stabilize;one pleasant result at a single hdoes not prove convergence. Near expiry/zero vol/payoff strike,derivatives can be singular or discontinuous and smooth asymptotics fail.

Some sources quote vega/rho per1percentage point and theta per day;this code deliberately returns per1.0and per year with explicit names. Macroption discusses both theta signs;its prose calls theta a time-to-expiry derivative but its displayed convention is elapsed-time decrease. We use explicit theta=-dV/dtauand compare that sign with finite differences. OIC warns Greeks are theoretical guideposts,not guaranteed exact premium changes. Do not copy a source's quote unit/sign without checking its definition. Positive/negative rate or put/call cases can change familiar theta signs.

Independent transfer:implement stated put Greeks and test call-minus-put delta=1,gamma/vega equality,rho difference=K*tau*D,and theta difference=-r*K*Dunder this no-dividend convention. Sweep valid central bumps for each Greek;include a tiny-hroundoff counterexample and a near-boundary case rejected by the interface. Reconcile position multiplier/sign and percent-point/basis-point conversions before using any sensitivity report. No local Greek creates live hedging authority or assures a risk-neutral portfolio in real markets.

Sources:[Macroption formula/unit/theta-convention discussion](https://www.macroption.com/black-scholes-formula/),[explicit Excel Greek formulas](https://www.macroption.com/option-greeks-excel/),[OIC guideposts and non-guarantee](https://www.optionseducation.org/advancedconcepts/understanding-options-greeks),[MITEuropean model](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-642-topics-in-mathematics-with-applications-in-finance-fall-2024/mit18_642_f24_lec21.pdf),and [Python math numerical functions](https://docs.python.org/3.12/library/math.html). Formula image pixels were inspected on a white background;source per100/day scaling is converted explicitly,not silently copied.

Reuse the derivation, not a tighter old API

The existing lesson derives the no-dividend European call Greeks. Its earlier helper rejects inputs when either d1 or d2 exceeds 8 in magnitude and uses spot>=1. The public task instead allows spot/strike>=.01 and only promises abs(d1)<8. Since d2=d1-sigma*sqrt(T), d2 can be below -8 while d1 is allowed. The separate greeks function honors that full public domain without calling the tighter old helper or changing it. Rates are continuous annual decimals;T is positive years and sigma is positive annualized decimal volatility,so zero-time/zero-vol limit branches are not public cases.

Four formulas and their units

Let w=sigma*sqrt(T),d1=(log(S/K)+(r+sigma^2/2)*T)/w,d2=d1-w,D=exp(-r*T),phi=exp(-d1^2/2)/sqrt(2*pi). Return C=S*Phi(d1)-K*D*Phi(d2),delta=Phi(d1),gamma=phi/(S*w),vega=S*phi*sqrt(T). The output order is price,delta,gamma,vega. Vega is per absolute volatility 1.00;per one percentage point would be this value times .01. No contract count or 100-share multiplier is supplied.

CDF and display policy

Evaluate Phi(x)=.5*erfc(-x/sqrt(2)) rather than1-Phi(-x) for a small negative tail. The direct call expression can still subtract nearby terms;the stated bounded smooth domain and independent high-precision comparisons are the source check,not a universal relative-accuracy guarantee for arbitrarily tiny premiums. Format only the final four values to six decimals,then canonicalize textual -0.000000 to 0.000000 as the public contract requires. This does not clamp a materially negative price or hide an invalid computation.

Trace, work and diagnostics

The standard S=K=100,r.05,sigma.2,T1 case prints10.450584 0.636831 0.018762 37.524035. q<=1000 gives O(q) fixed-size formula work and returned output. Compare price/CDF with a high-precision normal-series or integral implementation independent of math.erfc;compare derivatives with central-bump sweeps at supported interior points. Include S<1 and valid d1 with d2<-8to ensure no accidental old-API rejection. Price bounds,delta in[0,1] and nonnegative gamma/vega are diagnostics,not independent proof of every output digit or model fit. Passing this calculation grants no hedge or trade authority.

blocks.source:
from collections import OrderedDict, deque
from bisect import bisect_left
import heapq
import math
from fractions import Fraction

def greeks(queries):
    lines = []
    for (S, K, r, sigma, T) in queries:
        root = math.sqrt(T)
        width = sigma * root
        d1 = (math.log(S / K) + (r + sigma * sigma / 2) * T) / width
        d2 = d1 - width
        cdf1 = 0.5 * math.erfc(-d1 / math.sqrt(2))
        cdf2 = 0.5 * math.erfc(-d2 / math.sqrt(2))
        density = math.exp(-d1 * d1 / 2) / math.sqrt(2 * math.pi)
        call = S * cdf1 - K * math.exp(-r * T) * cdf2
        delta = cdf1
        gamma = density / (S * width)
        vega = S * density * root
        rendered = [f'{x:.6f}' for x in [call, delta, gamma, vega]]
        lines.append(' '.join(('0.000000' if text == '-0.000000' else text for text in rendered)))
    return lines

print(*greeks([(100.0,100.0,.05,.2,1.0),(100.0,110.0,0.0,.3,.5)]), sep='\n')
